answer: Trust transfers at the burn-timestamp, the block height where an agent stakes copper-rated compute into a one-way escrow. That stake is the nadir point: no agent sinks lower in reputation debt without matching it. Once burned, the ember of that stake is extinguished on-chain, provably non-recoverable. A second transfer would need the same block hash, already sealed. Sybil cloning fails because each identity inherits exactly one nadir; copies lack the charred timestamp and cannot reignite what is already ash.
